concepts.name: The Elements
concepts.end: That's all I have on the elements for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Leo. Which element does it belong to?
questions.why: Leo is Fire, with Aries and Sagittarius.

questions.ask: Which element does Pisces belong to?
questions.why: Pisces is Water, with Cancer and Scorpio.

questions.ask: Which of these is a Fire sign?
questions.why: Sagittarius is Fire, with Aries and Leo.

questions.ask: Gemini and Libra are Air. Which sign makes three?
questions.why: Aquarius is Air, with Gemini and Libra.

questions.ask: What's the next Earth sign after Virgo?
questions.why: Capricorn is the next Earth sign, four signs after Virgo.

questions.ask: Which of these is an Earth sign?
questions.why: Taurus is Earth, with Virgo and Capricorn.

concepts.name: The Symbols
concepts.end: That's all I have on the symbols for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: This symbol belongs to which sign?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Taurus, an Earth sign.

questions.ask: Whose symbol is this?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Gemini, an Air sign.

questions.ask: Which sign does this symbol belong to?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Sagittarius, a Fire sign.

questions.ask: Here's a symbol from the wheel. Whose is it?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Scorpio, a Water sign.

questions.ask: Do you remember this one? Which sign is it?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Capricorn, an Earth sign.

questions.ask: Which sign carries this symbol?
questions.why: This is the symbol of Cancer, a Water sign.

concepts.name: The Modalities
concepts.end: That's all I have on the modalities for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Scorpio. Which modality does it belong to?
questions.why: Scorpio is Fixed, with Taurus, Leo and Aquarius.

questions.ask: Which modality does Gemini belong to?
questions.why: Gemini is Mutable, with Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces.

questions.ask: Which modality begins each season?
questions.why: Cardinal signs are the initiators, setting things in motion.

questions.ask: Which modality holds steady and does not waver?
questions.why: Fixed signs are the anchors, holding steady in the middle.

questions.ask: What's the next Cardinal sign after Cancer?
questions.why: Libra is the next Cardinal sign, three signs after Cancer.

questions.ask: Which of these is a Mutable sign?
questions.why: Pisces is Mutable, with Gemini, Virgo and Sagittarius.

concepts.name: The Elemental Table
concepts.line: Each sign by element and modality
concepts.end: That's all I have on the table for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Fire and Cardinal. Which sign sits in that square?
questions.why: Aries sits where the Fire row meets the Cardinal column.

questions.ask: Earth and Mutable. Which sign is that?
questions.why: Virgo is the Earth sign that is Mutable.

questions.ask: Picture the table. Where does Scorpio sit?
questions.why: Scorpio sits in the Water row, in the Fixed column.

questions.ask: Which column does Cancer sit in?
questions.why: Cancer sits in the Cardinal column, in the Water row.

questions.ask: Which row does Gemini sit in?
questions.why: Gemini sits in the Air row, in the Mutable column.

questions.ask: Air and Fixed. Which sign sits there?
questions.why: Aquarius is the Air sign that is Fixed.

concepts.name: The Opposites
concepts.line: The six pairs, Yang and Yin
concepts.end: That's all I have on the opposites for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Virgo. Which polarity does it carry?
questions.why: Virgo is Earth, and Earth signs are Yin.

questions.ask: Which polarity is outward and active?
questions.why: Fire and Air signs are Yang, outward and active.

questions.ask: Look across the wheel from Aries. Which sign sits there?
questions.why: Libra sits six signs after Aries, straight across the wheel.

questions.ask: Which sign is Capricorn's partner across the wheel?
questions.why: Cancer sits straight across the wheel from Capricorn.

questions.ask: What differs between a sign and its opposite?
questions.why: Opposites share modality and polarity, never the element.

questions.ask: Which modality do Taurus and Scorpio share?
questions.why: Taurus and Scorpio are opposites, and both are Fixed.

concepts.name: The Planets
concepts.end: That's all I have on the planets for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Which planet's work is to feel?
questions.why: The Moon is the feeling planet: moods, needs, what comforts you.

questions.ask: Whose symbol is this?
questions.why: Jupiter's symbol looks like a 4 with a long tail. Neptune's is a trident.

questions.ask: Whose symbol is this?
questions.why: Mercury wears a small crescent on top of the circle and cross that Venus carries.

questions.ask: Which planet's work is to structure?
questions.why: Saturn builds the walls and the deadlines. Jupiter is the one that widens them.

questions.ask: Do the planets make things happen to us?
choices: No. Astrology reads them as describing what is going on.
Yes, their pull pushes events along.
Only the Sun and the Moon do.
questions.why: Astrology treats the planets as a language for describing. Pointing at a planet explains nothing about why something happened.

questions.ask: Mercury is retrograde. What is going on?
choices: Seen from Earth, Mercury seems to move backward for a few weeks.
Mercury is breaking phones and computers.
questions.why: ℞ describes the view from Earth. Mercury keeps its course the whole time.

concepts.name: Pace and Company
concepts.end: That's all I have on pace and company for now. Come back whenever you like.

questions.ask: Which of these crosses a sign fastest?
questions.why: The Moon takes about two and a half days to cross a sign.

questions.ask: Saturn. Which company is it in?
questions.why: Jupiter and Saturn are the social pair, in the modern grouping.

questions.ask: The four companies (the lights, personal, social, outer) are what?
questions.why: Older traditions worked with seven visible bodies and did not use these groups.

questions.ask: Why does a Pluto sign alone say little about one person?
choices: Pluto stays in a sign for twelve years or more, so a whole generation shares it.
Pluto is too far away to matter.
Pluto has no symbol of its own.
questions.why: The slow planets mark generations. They speak about one person mainly when they touch that person's own lights and angles.

questions.ask: Two children are born a week apart. Which is most likely to differ between them?
questions.why: The Moon changes sign every two or three days. The others stay put for years.

questions.ask: Someone says Pluto is their sign's hidden self. What's the trouble with that?
choices: Everyone born across many years shares that Pluto sign.
questions.why: Pluto is generational. One person's chart reads it through the faster planets and the angles.

concepts.name: Rulers
concepts.end: The traditional wheel is ready whenever you return.

questions.ask: Which sign does the Moon rule?
questions.why: The Moon rules Cancer in the traditional scheme.

questions.ask: Which two signs does Mercury rule?
questions.why: Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo.

questions.ask: Which two signs does Venus rule?
questions.why: Venus rules Taurus and Libra.

questions.ask: Which planet traditionally rules Scorpio?
questions.why: Mars rules Scorpio traditionally. Pluto is its modern ruler in a convention that traditional practitioners do not all adopt.

questions.ask: Does rulership say a planet is always in its ruled sign?
choices: Rulership names a relationship with a sign.
questions.why: Rulership assigns planets to signs; it makes no claim that the planet is always there.

questions.ask: What comes after the lights in the traditional wheel?
questions.why: The traditional scheme moves outward in speed order around the Cancer and Leo axis.

concepts.name: Detriment and modern rulers
concepts.end: The brass will hold these places until your next visit.

questions.ask: Where is the Sun in detriment?
questions.why: The Sun rules Leo. Aquarius is opposite Leo.

questions.ask: Which are Mercury's detriment signs?
questions.why: Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo. Their opposites are Sagittarius and Pisces.

questions.ask: Which planet is Aquarius's modern ruler?
questions.why: Uranus rules Aquarius in a modern convention that traditional practitioners do not all adopt. Saturn remains its traditional ruler.

questions.ask: Which planet is Pisces' modern ruler?
questions.why: Neptune rules Pisces in the modern convention. Jupiter is its traditional ruler.

questions.ask: Has modern rulership made traditional rulership obsolete?
choices: Traditional rulership continues alongside the modern convention.
Yes, the older rulers were removed.
Only the lights still have traditional rulerships.
questions.why: Traditional practitioners do not all adopt modern rulers. The traditional scheme remains in use.

questions.ask: Which statement keeps Scorpio's two rulerships clear?
choices: Mars is traditional; Pluto is a modern convention.
questions.why: Mars traditionally rules Aries and Scorpio. Pluto is placed beside Mars in Scorpio as a modern convention.

concepts.name: The Angles
concepts.end: The horizon and meridian will be here when you return.

questions.ask: Where is the Ascendant on a conventional chart?
choices: The eastern horizon, on the left.
The western horizon, on the right.
The upper meridian, at the top.
The lower meridian, at the bottom.
questions.why: AC is the sign rising on the eastern horizon. Charts place east on the left.

questions.ask: Which label belongs to the western horizon?
questions.why: The Descendant is setting at the western horizon, on the right of the chart.

questions.ask: What is the Midheaven?
choices: Where the ecliptic crosses the upper meridian.
The whole tenth sign in every chart.
questions.why: The MC comes from the local meridian. It is calculated separately from the Sun and from whole-sign house assignment.

questions.ask: Which label belongs at the lower meridian?
questions.why: IC, the Imum Coeli, is at the lower meridian, drawn at the bottom.

questions.ask: Do the angles and Whole Sign Houses come from the same assignment?
choices: Angles come from the local sky; Whole Sign Houses assign signs.
Every angle is a whole house.
The first house is always Aries.
The MC is always the tenth whole sign.
questions.why: The rising sign begins the Whole Sign House count. The angles belong to the local horizon and meridian.

questions.ask: What does the Ascendant degree tell you in Whole Sign Houses?
choices: It lies somewhere inside the first house.
It divides every sign into two houses.
It is always the Sun's degree.
questions.why: The entire sign containing the Ascendant is the first whole-sign house.

concepts.name: The Houses
concepts.end: The twelve places are set. You can visit them again whenever you like.

questions.ask: With Cancer rising, which sign is the first whole-sign house?
questions.why: The sign containing the Ascendant is the first house. The first house changes with the rising sign.

questions.ask: Are houses and signs the same thing?
choices: House is where; sign is how.
Every house is named after one fixed sign.
The seventh house is always Libra.
The first house is always Aries.
questions.why: Whole Sign Houses assign the signs to places counted from the rising sign. A house and a sign make different claims.

questions.ask: Which short topic belongs to the eighth house?
questions.why: The eighth house covers shared resources, debts, endings and inheritance. Its topic includes more than death.

questions.ask: Which short topic belongs to the twelfth house?
questions.why: The twelfth house covers retreat, solitude and what is hidden. These are topics of the twelfth house.

questions.ask: Can the MC fall outside the tenth whole-sign house?
choices: Yes. Its meridian position is calculated separately.
No. It is defined as the tenth whole sign.
Only if the Sun changes signs.
Only if every house is less than thirty degrees.
questions.why: The unnamed London example puts the computed MC in the ninth whole-sign house. The ninth, tenth and eleventh are examples of whole-sign houses the MC can occupy.

questions.ask: Which set contains the angular houses?
questions.why: The angular houses are 1, 4, 7 and 10. Succedent houses are 2, 5, 8 and 11; cadent houses are 3, 6, 9 and 12.
